Sentence (English): Bought and installed this dishwasher in mid-August, and it performed well for about six weeks, when it started throwing a code indicating a leak.
Comments (English): [ Very disappointed in Lowe's ] || ---------------- || Bought and installed this dishwasher in mid-August, and it performed well for about six weeks, when it started throwing a code indicating a leak. Following LG's troubleshooting guidelines, I restarted the machine and it cleared the code for another week or so, when it returned. This time I called LG and they sent a service tech to inspect the dishwasher. He told me the leak, in the top corner of the tub, was clearly a result of damage in shipping or warehousing at Lowe's, and LG would not cover the repair under warranty. At this point, I initiated a case (I thought) with Lowe's customer service. After several days of explaining and re-explaining to roughly four different representatives, I was told they were sending a technician to inspect the damage and fix it if possible. When the "technicians" arrived (on schedule and very understanding, to their credit, but actually delivery workers) I was told they didn't know exactly why they were there, as they were expecting to deliver an appliance. I provided them with copies of the LG tech's report and they assured me they would put it with my file(? ). At this point, I basically had to start over with customer service. After being told that I must have damaged the dishwasher because I didn't notice the damage within 48 hours, I was finally handed off to someone with more authority, and after an hour or so on the phone, I was told their hands were tied, but she had talked to the manager of my store, who would be reaching out to me within 24 hours to discuss options. This never happened. Lowe's, instead of standing behind their merchandise, kept the balls in the air until I gave up and fixed the leak myself. To sum it up, I paid $700 for a broken dishwasher that I had to fix myself after weeks of phone calls and empty rhetoric.

Sentence (English): We bought this dishwasher about a month ago to replace our old trusty KitchenAid KUDE70FVSS2, which had finally stopped working after many, many years.
Comments (English): [ Good cleaning, but poorly designed shelves ] || ---------------- || We bought this dishwasher about a month ago to replace our old trusty KitchenAid KUDE70FVSS2, which had finally stopped working after many, many years. We loved the layout of that old unit. Not so much the new. Many of our items that fit perfectly in the older dishwasher, simply don't fit or don't fit easily into the new. Why change the shelf layouts so much? The new one has no middle rack flip down shelf (to hold small plastic ware items below, and additional spoons etc. above. Just one example. Sentence (English): I bought this dishwasher to replace an older Whirlpool model.
Comments (English): [ 3 weeks in and here is what I think ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher to replace an older Whirlpool model. We chose this one based on Consumer Reports' claims about its superior drying performance, our curiosity about the third rack, and overall brand reputation. We've had it for about three weeks now, and here are my thoughts so far—what I like, what I don't, and what might influence whether I'd buy it again.What I Like -• It does an excellent job cleaning, which is expected for a new unit, but still nice to see confirmed in practice.• The third rack is handy for various items. Since I've never had one before, I sometimes forget it's there, but it's a nice bonus once you get used to using it.What I Don't Like - • The dishwasher has a slight lean to it and doesn't sit perfectly flush with the surrounding cabinetry. Installation seems correct and it's level, so it might just be how the unit is built. Not a deal-breaker—just a bit odd.• The handle sticks out, which is typical for KitchenAid. It looks fine, but it does take away from a more streamlined look. Again, not a big deal, just slightly annoying.• The silverware basket on the bottom rack isn't secured, so it slides around. Some people might like the flexibility, but I personally find it frustrating. I prefer everything to stay in place. Not a deal-breaker• The door is pretty stiff when opening. I'm guessing it'll loosen up over time, but right now it takes a bit of force to pull down when loading the bottom rack. On the plus side, at least it doesn't flop open on its own—that would be worse. Lastly, not a big deal, just annoying.Overall -So far, it seems like a solid, well-performing dishwasher. It cleans well, but a few design quirks keep it from being perfect. Only time will tell how it holds up long-term.

Comments (English): [ Decent Dishwasher Grossly Overpriced. ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is no better than the 10 yr old Maytag it replaced. The DW is very quiet. It cleans well and has plenty of functional options. The third rack on top is a good idea that doesn't really work. With the middle rack in the upper position, my tervis tumblers drag on top rack. With the middle rack on the lower setting, the middle rack drags on the dinner plates on the bottom. I tried many times to make this work. Eventually, I removed the top rack. If there was an intermediate height setting on the middle rack, it might have worked. Also, the middle rack doesn't slide out very smoothly. It has a noticeable drag about halfway out. The utensil caddy so/so. There are plenty of slots, but the utensils tend to get stuck in the holes making it difficult to remove them. After a week of using the DW, I had to call the installer to come back and reattach the DW to the cabinet. The flimsy tabs used to secure the DW came loose on the top support. Installer indicated this was a common problem and design flaw. The DW is very attractive. Hoping it lives up to its reputation for reliability. If it cost three times as much but only last twice as long, that's not a good value.

Sentence (English): I extensively shopped for a new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Not a homerun for me ] || ---------------- || I extensively shopped for a new dishwasher. I have only had Kenmore dishwashers (all had been manufactured by Whirlpool starting with our first purchase in 2000). I have loved them, there have been three in total with the most recent one lasting us about 8 years. I was raising a family, so many times our dishwasher ran 2x per day. Well it finally gave up on us so I began the search for a new one. Looking at the local big box stores as well as local appliance stores. I still preferred the layout of the Whirlpool brand products which includes Maytag and KitchenAid. The one hurdle was it had to be black, apparently stainless is still popular and some models are only made in stainless. I finally settled on this Maytag because the rack layout was like what I wanted and very much the same as my prior Kenmore dishwashers and seemed sturdy with not many bells and whistles (I just need it to wash and dry our dishes). I was giddy with excitement after waiting 3 weeks for the dishwasher to arrive. Well first off, the bottom rack was different than the one in the store. The rack I received was missing two rows of tines, which I use very much to put my 9x13 pans or tuck extra bowls in. Thankfully I kept the racks from my old dishwasher so it was an easy swap with the bottom rack (tho we ended up having to swap the wheels because my old rack rode a little higher making it too tall for some things in the silverware basket). Sadly I hate the top rack too and there is no way to swap my old rack out with the one in this model because the shape is entirely different. That is my beef with this dishwasher, the top rack! Compared to my old rack, it has two less tines per row and the higher center row doming up makes things not want to stay put (mainly plastic lids want to flop over). It is driving me batty! The dishwasher cleans well, but I am not really pleased with the layout. Whoever changed the racks, doesn't use the appliance apparently. I'm not sure how long I'll forge ahead with this dishwasher. I'm really trying to give it an honest go, but after 10 days of use, I still hate the top rack and feel like it just doesn't hold that many items like my old rack did. And really the silverware rack is dumb too because it has two large open compartments in addition to the two compartments with slits for utensils. The two larger open compartments (my old one had three that were narrower) makes it hard to get larger cooking utensils to stand up, they want to fall over and nest together. I feel like I wasted my husband's hard earned $$ on this dishwasher. It does clean well, but the layout is so annoying to me and I'm just not sure how long I can look past it. I may be shopping for a new dishwasher yet again and list this on Craigslist. Super disappointing. Possibly if I had gotten the one with the 3rd rack I'd be happier because I could put larger utensils and plastic lids there, but that was out of stock at the time. I was so hopeful that I really did my due diligence by going to the local stores to look at dishwashers, but I guess there are other things I didn't consider. I will reiterate again, it does clean well and it very roomy inside to have tall things on both the upper and lower rack, so it does have that going for it.

The rack I received was missing two rows of tines, which I use very much to put my 9x13 pans or tuck extra bowls in.  Thankfully I kept the racks from my old dishwasher so it was an easy swap with the bottom rack (tho we ended up having to swap the wheels because my old rack rode a little higher making it too tall for some things in the silverware basket).  Sadly I hate the top rack too and there is no way to swap my old rack out with the one in this model because the shape is entirely different.  That is my beef with this dishwasher, the top rack!  Compared to my old rack, it has two less tines per row and the higher center row doming up makes things not want to stay put (mainly plastic lids want to flop over).  It is driving me batty!  The dishwasher cleans well, but I am not really pleased with the layout.  Whoever changed the racks, doesn't use the appliance apparently.  I'm not sure how long I'll forge ahead with this dishwasher.  I'm really trying to give it an honest go, but after 10 days of use, I still hate the top rack and feel like it just doesn't hold that many items like my old rack did.  And really the silverware rack is dumb too because it has two large open compartments in addition to the two compartments with slits for utensils.  The two larger open compartments (my old one had three that were narrower) makes it hard to get larger cooking utensils to stand up, they want to fall over and nest together.  I feel like I wasted my husband's hard earned $$ on this dishwasher.  It does clean well, but the layout is so annoying to me and I'm just not sure how long I can look past it.  I may be shopping for a new dishwasher yet again and list this on Craigslist.  Super disappointing. Possibly if I had gotten the one with the 3rd rack I'd be happier because I could put larger utensils and plastic lids there, but that was out of stock at the time.  I was so hopeful that I really did my due diligence by going to the local stores to look at dishwashers, but I guess there are other things I didn't consider.  I will reiterate again, it does clean well and it very roomy inside to have tall things on both the upper and lower rack, so it does have that going for it.

Comments (English): [ 3 weeks in and here is what I think ] || ---------------- || I bought this dishwasher to replace an older Whirlpool model. We chose this one based on Consumer Reports' claims about its superior drying performance, our curiosity about the third rack, and overall brand reputation. We've had it for about three weeks now, and here are my thoughts so far—what I like, what I don't, and what might influence whether I'd buy it again. What I Like -. • It does an excellent job cleaning, which is expected for a new unit, but still nice to see confirmed in practice. • The third rack is handy for various items. Since I've never had one before, I sometimes forget it's there, but it's a nice bonus once you get used to using it. What I Don't Like - . • The dishwasher has a slight lean to it and doesn't sit perfectly flush with the surrounding cabinetry. Installation seems correct and it's level, so it might just be how the unit is built. Not a deal-breaker—just a bit odd. • The handle sticks out, which is typical for KitchenAid. It looks fine, but it does take away from a more streamlined look. Again, not a big deal, just slightly annoying. • The silverware basket on the bottom rack isn't secured, so it slides around. Some people might like the flexibility, but I personally find it frustrating. I prefer everything to stay in place. Not a deal-breaker. • The door is pretty stiff when opening. I'm guessing it'll loosen up over time, but right now it takes a bit of force to pull down when loading the bottom rack. On the plus side, at least it doesn't flop open on its own—that would be worse. Lastly, not a big deal, just annoying. Overall -. So far, it seems like a solid, well-performing dishwasher. It cleans well, but a few design quirks keep it from being perfect. Only time will tell how it holds up long-term.

We’ve had it for about three weeks now, and here are my thoughts so far—what I like, what I don’t, and what might influence whether I’d buy it again.What I Like -• It does an excellent job cleaning, which is expected for a new unit, but still nice to see confirmed in practice.• The third rack is handy for various items. Since I’ve never had one before, I sometimes forget it’s there, but it’s a nice bonus once you get used to using it.What I Don’t Like - • The dishwasher has a slight lean to it and doesn’t sit perfectly flush with the surrounding cabinetry. Installation seems correct and it’s level, so it might just be how the unit is built. Not a deal-breaker—just a bit odd.• The handle sticks out, which is typical for KitchenAid. It looks fine, but it does take away from a more streamlined look. Again, not a big deal, just slightly annoying.• The silverware basket on the bottom rack isn’t secured, so it slides around. Some people might like the flexibility, but I personally find it frustrating. I prefer everything to stay in place. Not a deal-breaker• The door is pretty stiff when opening. I’m guessing it’ll loosen up over time, but right now it takes a bit of force to pull down when loading the bottom rack. On the plus side, at least it doesn’t flop open on its own—that would be worse. Lastly, not a big deal, just annoying.Overall -So far, it seems like a solid, well-performing dishwasher. It cleans well, but a few design quirks keep it from being perfect. Only time will tell how it holds up long-term.

Sentence (English): I was looking for a compact dishwasher for newlyweds or single- or two-person households, and I finally got it at the perfect time.
Comments (English): I was looking for a compact dishwasher for newlyweds or single- or two-person households, and I finally got it at the perfect time. What I liked most was the no-drill installation. No need to drill holes in the wall or sink. Simply fill the tank, which significantly reduced installation hassle. My faucet is a Cobra, so I simply plugged it in and filled it with water. However, my first impression upon receiving the dishwasher was that it's actually larger than it looks in the photos! The interior is also quite compact for its size. While it's rated for three people, it's only big enough for two people's worth of dishes and utensils. Larger cookware like pans and pots won't fit. However, I was very satisfied with the cleaning performance. It cleaned dishes and glasses with soup stains and grease cleanly. The drying performance is also quite good. Because it uses high temperature water, it dries quickly and fluffily after washing. So, when I cook, I just turn it once for the cooking utensils, and after eating, I turn it twice for the dishes. The noise is hardly bothersome, and it is simple to use, so I think even the elderly can use it without difficulty. Overall: It has a small size, a clean appearance, and the strong advantage of non-perforated installation, and the cleaning power is satisfactory. I recommend it for small kitchens of 1-2 people rather than large families!
Comments (Original): 신혼부부나 1~2인 가구를 위한 컴팩트한 식기세척기를 찾았는데 마침 좋은 기회로 겟했어요 가장 마음에 들었던 건 무타공 설치라는 점인데요 벽이나 싱크대에 구멍을 뚫지 않아도 되고, 물통만 채워 사용하니 설치에 대한 부담이 확실히 덜했습니다  우리집은 코브라 수전이라서 그냥 수전 끝고와서 만수될때까지 채웠어요 다만 제품을 처음 받아보고 느낀 건, 사진으로 봤을 때보다 실제로는 크다는 점!. 그리고 크기에 비해 내부는 작아요 3인용이라고는 하지만 실사용 기준으로는  2인분 정도 식기와 조리도구를 넣으면 딱 맞는 정도예요. 팬이나 냄비 같은 부파 큰 조리기구는 들어가기 어려워요 하지만! 세척력은 정말 만족스러웠습니다. 국물 자국, 기름7 있는 접시나 유리컵도 뽀득뽀득하게 잘 씻겨 나옵니다. 건조 성능도 꽤 괜찮은 편이고요.  고온수라서 그런지 세척 후에는 빠르게 뽀송뽀송하게 잘 마름니다 그래서 그냥 요리할때 나온 조리도구 한번 돌리고 밥먹고나면 먹은 그릇돌리고 두번돌려요 소음도 거의 거슬리지 않고. 조작도 간단해서 어르신들도 어렵지 않게 사용하실 수 있을 것 같아요. 총평: 작은 사이즈에 깔끔한 외형, 무타공 설치라는 장점이 강하고 세척력도 만족스럽습니다. 대가족보다는 1~2인 가구 소형 주방에 추천!

Sentence (English): [Coupang Experience Group Review] This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event.
Comments (English): [ Minix Mini Dishwasher PRO 3-Person ] || ---------------- || [Coupang Experience Group Review] This review was written after receiving a free product as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. Maximizing the efficiency of a small kitchen! As a Coupang Experience Group member, I got to try out the MINIX Mini Dishwasher PRO 3-Person. Although I live in a 2-3-person household, my kitchen space is limited, so I hesitated to install a dishwasher. This product, with its no-installation/no-drill design and compact size, maximized space efficiency. Despite its small size, all the main functions worked perfectly, making it a very satisfying experience. The freedom of no-installation/no-drill design: Suitable for any kitchen. The biggest advantage of the MINIX PRO model is its no-installation design, requiring no water connection or plumbing. Simply plug it in and refill the water tank directly, allowing me to place it freely in a small corner next to the sink. Optimized for small spaces, its clean design doesn't detract from the kitchen's interior, but rather adds a touch of sophistication. Powerful Cleaning Power and Dual Nozzle System: I was a bit concerned about the 3-person capacity, but my concerns were completely dispelled after using it. Dual rotating nozzles located at the top and bottom deliver a powerful stream of water without any blind spots, ensuring exceptional cleaning power. Even a rice bowl with stuck-on rice and a greasy pork stir-fry dish were squeakily clean on the "Strong" cycle without pre-washing. The addition of a high-temperature sterilization function further enhances hygiene. The innovative "Auto Door Open & Standalone Drying" feature in this mini dishwasher is truly innovative. After washing, the door automatically opens, effectively discharging moisture and residual steam, and promoting drying. This feature eliminates the hassle of leaving the door open after washing and eliminates the worry of water pooling on dishes and causing odors. Furthermore, a standalone drying mode, without washing, is a highly useful feature for quickly drying and sterilizing wet cups and cutting boards. Smart Convenience and Economical MINIX PRO offers six different washing modes, allowing for optimal cleaning depending on the type and level of soiling of your dishes. In addition, it only uses 5.5L of water per wash and consumes less power than a 6-person product, which is excellent for saving water and electricity. Even though it is an installation-free product, it is intuitively designed with convenient features such as a full water alarm, so even users who are not familiar with using machines can use it easily. Overall Review: The perfect kitchen revolution for 1-3 person households The Minix Mini Dishwasher PRO 3-person is a great product that has it all: the convenience of installation-free/no drilling, the powerful cleaning power of the upper and lower nozzles, and the innovative features of the automatic door opening and independent drying mode. For 1-3 person households that have given up on a dishwasher due to limited kitchen space, I highly recommend this product as the most practical and effective alternative that will free you from the chore of washing dishes.

Sentence (English): Regarding product configuration and delivery, I purchased a 12-seater dishwasher from Mydia.
Comments (English): Regarding product configuration and delivery, I purchased a 12-seater dishwasher from Mydia. I chose silver, although black was also available. Since it's a dishwasher, it's bound to get wet, so I decided to go with silver to protect against water stains. It was a good choice, and the more I use it, the more I appreciate it. The complete package includes the dishwasher itself, a manual, a drain hose, and brackets for connecting various hoses. It's a complete package, comparable to other brands of dishwashers on the market. Because it's a rocket-installed product, the installer personally visited and completed the installation. Simply specifying the installation location allowed the installation to be completed in about 15 minutes, making it quick and easy to install. As mentioned briefly above, the installer personally visited the customer service center, brought the product to the customer, and simply provided the location for installation. I originally planned to install it as a built-in unit, but upon seeing the product, I realized it came with a freestanding configuration, so I ended up installing it that way. The installer even kindly explained that I only needed to remove the top panel to install it as a built-in unit, which made me feel like I had a really pleasant installation. The installer was very friendly, and although the installation must have been difficult, he provided detailed instructions, including explanations of each device's functions. Since it's a product that you just plug in after installation, I think it won't be difficult to install if you move or relocate later. It looks easier than I thought. These days, it seems like a lot of home appliances are switching to touchscreens. While touchscreens have their advantages, I think it's safer to use physical buttons on home appliances like dishwashers to prevent malfunctions or accidental touches, which is why I chose this product. The buttons are divided into physical buttons, which is good for preventing malfunctions during operation. The buttons are sturdy and the design is pretty enough to compare with dishwashers from more expensive famous brands. The silver color is the same as on the product page, but it felt like a toned-down gray in person. It looks more modern and calm than I thought, so I really liked the color. My thoughts while using it After actually using it, the 12-person dishwasher was a dishwasher with enough capacity to load and run all the dishes used for one meal for a family of about 4-5 people at once. It was hard to estimate because the capacity was written as 12 or 14 people, but after actually using it, I think a 12-person dishwasher would be perfect for a household of 3-4 people. It is a cost-effective dishwasher, but the quality and performance are just as good as those of famous brands. It washes the dishes perfectly, leaves them fluffy, and is perfect! If you are looking for a cost-effective product that is faithful to the original function of a dishwasher, I would like to recommend this product completely. Sentence (English): Regarding the product configuration and delivery, I purchased a 12-seater dishwasher from Mydia.
Comments (English): Regarding the product configuration and delivery, I purchased a 12-seater dishwasher from Mydia. I purchased the silver color, although black was also available. Since it's a dishwasher, it's bound to get wet, so I chose silver to protect against water stains. It was a good choice, and the more I use it, the more I appreciate it. The complete package includes the dishwasher itself, a manual, a drain hose, and brackets for connecting various hoses. It's a complete package, comparable to other brands of dishwashers on the market. Because it's a rocket-installed product, the installer personally visited and completed the installation. Simply specifying the installation location allowed the installation to be completed in about 15 minutes, making it quick and easy to install. The installation process: As mentioned above, the installer personally visited, brought the product, and simply provided the location, allowing for immediate installation. I originally planned to install it as a built-in unit, but upon seeing the product, I realized it came with a freestanding configuration, so I ended up installing it that way. The installer even kindly explained that I only needed to remove the top panel to install it as a built-in unit, which made the installation quite pleasant. The installer was very friendly, and although the installation must have been difficult, he provided detailed instructions, including explanations of each device's functions. Since it's essentially a plug-and-play product, I think it'll be easy to install even if I move or relocate later. It looks easier than I thought. Design. These days, it seems like a lot of home appliances are switching to touchscreens. While touchscreens have their advantages, I think physical buttons are safer for home appliances like dishwashers to prevent malfunctions or accidental touches, which is why I chose this product. The buttons are divided into physical buttons, which is good for preventing malfunctions during operation. The buttons are sturdy and the design is pretty enough to compare with dishwashers from more expensive famous brands. The silver color is the same as on the product page, but it felt like a toned-down gray in person. It looks more modern and calm than I thought, so I really liked the color. My thoughts while using it. When I actually used it, the 12-person dishwasher was more than enough to load and run all the dishes used for one meal for a family of about 4-5 people at once, and there was still some left. The capacity was difficult to estimate because it was written that the dishwasher was for 12 or 14 people, but after actually using it, I think a 12-person dishwasher would be just right for a household of 3-4 people. It is a cost-effective dishwasher, but the quality and performance are just as good as those of famous brands. It washes the dishes perfectly, leaving them fluffy and perfect! If this level of detail is missing and the price is low, this much is forgivable. The installer was very kind, and the E4 error may appear occasionally during use. Sentence (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.
Comments (Original): 결론부터 말하면, “왜 이제야 식세기 입문했나…” 싶은 제품이에요. LG 디오스 오브제컬렉션 빌트인 14인용으로 첫 식기세척기 들이면서 느낀 점들 정리해볼게요. 1. 디자인 & 빌트인 만족도 네이처 베이지 색상이 진짜 과하지 않은 은은한 톤이라 주방 가구랑 자연스럽게 잘 섞여요.  손잡이, 로고 다 심플해서 눈에 안 띄고, 문 닫아두면 그냥 한 칸의 장처럼 보여서 깔끔합니다.  빌트인 설치라 동선 방해도 없고, 기존 싱크 옆 수납장 하나 빼고 쏙 들어가서 공간 활용 면에서도 만족.  2. 용량 & 내부 구조  14인용이라 처음엔 “우리 집에 너무 큰 거 아닌가?” 했는데, 써보니까 이 정도는 돼야 한 끼 설거지 모아서 한 번에 돌리기 좋더라구요.  상단(컵/머그/소형 볼), 중단(그릇/찬기), 하단(냄비/팬/도마) 구조로 되어 있고, 칸칸이 높이 조절, 접이식 바스켓이 있어서 집마다 쓰는 그릇 형태에 맞게 조금씩 세팅해두면 편해요.  밥공기, 국그릇, 접시, 유리컵, 아이 식판까지 꽉 채워도 한 번에 들어가는 날이 많아서, 손 설거지로 치면 제법 “산더미 설거지”를 기계 한 번으로 끝내는 느낌입니다.  3. 세척력 (가장 중요한 부분)  기름기 많은 프라이팬, 불고기 양념 그릇, 카레/찌개 그릇까지 테스트해봤는데, 예열 없이 그냥 넣어도 거의 말끔하게 나옵니다.  사용 팁:  음식물만 살짝 털어내고 넣으면 되고, 굳이 박박 헹굴 필요 없어요.  너무 눌어붙은 건 (특히 계란, 치즈) 살짝만 불려서 넣으면 실패 없이 잘 떨어져요.  유리컵에 남던 물자국, 뿌연 막 같은 것도 거의 없어져서 컵이 새것처럼 반짝하는 게 확실히 느껴집니다.  4. 건조 & 냄새  건조 코스까지 돌리면 상온에 꺼내뒀을 때랑 비슷한 정도로 잘 말라 있어요. (바닥 면적 넓은 플라스틱 밀폐용기는 물방울 조금 남는 정도)  문이 자동으로 살짝 열리면서 열기 빼주는 기능 덕분인지 눅눅한 냄새, 비린내 거의 없습니다.  내부에서 나는 플라스틱 탑 노즐 냄새도 초반 몇 번 사용 이후엔 신경 안 쓰일 정도.  5. 소음 & 사용 편의성  돌릴 때 소음은 “세탁기 탈수” 기준으로 보면 한참 덜 하고, 거실에서 TV 보는 데 방해 안 되는 수준이라 밤에도 돌리기 괜찮아요.  조작부가 상단에 깔끔하게 모여 있고, 코스 선택도 직관적이라 처음 식세기 입문해도 설명서 한 번 보면 바로 감 잡습니다.  문 열고 닫힐 때 느낌이 탄탄해서 오래 쓸 수 있겠다 싶어요.  6. 물/시간/멘탈 절약 효과  한 번에 돌리면 물 사용량이 손 설거지보다 적다고 해서 골랐는데, 실제로 설거지통에 물 잔뜩 틀어놓고 하던 버릇 생각하면 심리적으로도 절약하는 기분이에요.  가장 큰 장점은 시간 & 체력 세이브. 식사 후 설거지 산처럼 쌓여 있어도 그냥 기계에 차곡차곡 넣고 버튼 한 번. 저녁마다 설거지 생각에 한숨 쉬던 게 사라져서, 이게 진짜 삶의 질 차이구나 싶습니다.  7. 아쉬운 점(솔직하게)  처음 설치할 땐 빌트인이다 보니 설치 일정, 주방 사이즈 체크를 꼼꼼히 봐야 해서 살짝 번거롭긴 했어요. Sentence (English): The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.
