Sentence (English): The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Sentence (English): If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.
Comments (English): To cut to the chase, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just started buying a dishwasher now. Let me summarize my thoughts on the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-seater dishwasher. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction: The nature beige color is a subtle, understated tone that blends in well with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and discreet, and when the door is closed, it looks like a single cabinet, giving it a clean, uncluttered look. Because it's built-in, it doesn't obstruct movement, and it fits in the cabinet next to the existing sink, making for a satisfying space utilization. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure: At first, I thought the 14-seater capacity was too big for my home, but after using it, I realized it's just the right size for collecting and washing dishes for one meal at a time. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has an adjustable height and a foldable basket, so it's convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the type of dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates at once, so it feels like I'm finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with just one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tip: Just lightly shake off the food before putting it in, and there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. For things that are stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak them slightly and they come off without fail. The water marks and cloudy film that used to remain on the glass cups are almost gone, so you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor: When I run it through the drying cycle, it's almost as dry as when I left it out at room temperature. (In plastic airtight containers with a large bottom, only a few drops of water remain.) Thanks to the automatic door opening function that slightly releases heat, there's almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle odor from inside became unnoticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease: The noise level is much lower than that of a typical washing machine spin cycle, and it's quiet enough not to disturb TV viewing in the living room, making it comfortable to use even at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even a first-time dishwasher user will get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I expect it to last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this product because it's said to use less water per cycle than washing dishes by hand. And considering how much water I used to leave running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving a lot of money. The biggest advantage is the time and energy savings. Even after a meal, the dishes pile up like a mountain, but I just load them neatly into the dishwasher and press a button. The sighs I used to feel over the thought of washing dishes every evening are gone, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly): When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because it was a built-in unit, so I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size. (Still, I was satisfied that the installer neatly finished it to the right size.) While it has ample storage, I still haven't gotten used to it, so it took a while to arrange it at first. After a few tries, I developed a template for the internal layout that matches my household dish patterns, and now it's automatic. Overall, I'm very satisfied with this product, as it addressed all my concerns about cleaning power, noise, and design when I first bought a dishwasher. If you want to coordinate your kitchen with a consistent daily load, you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-seater built-in.

Then, when I was exposed to dishwashers by an algorithm, I decided I had to buy one. There were plenty of candidates for a six-person dishwasher. The price was reasonable, and after looking at Cuckoo, SK, and Samsung, I realized they were all manufactured at the MyDeer factory in Foshan, China. My current induction cooktop is a Rinnai, but it's a MyDeer-branded one. My recent all-in-one oven was also a MyDeer, so I looked for the cheapest option and found this one. If this level of detail is missing and the price is low, this much is forgivable. The installer was very kind, and the E4 error may appear occasionally during use. Sentence (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.
Comments (Original): 결론부터 말하면, “왜 이제야 식세기 입문했나…” 싶은 제품이에요.LG 디오스 오브제컬렉션 빌트인 14인용으로 첫 식기세척기 들이면서 느낀 점들 정리해볼게요.1. 디자인 & 빌트인 만족도네이처 베이지 색상이 진짜 과하지 않은 은은한 톤이라 주방 가구랑 자연스럽게 잘 섞여요.손잡이, 로고 다 심플해서 눈에 안 띄고, 문 닫아두면 그냥 한 칸의 장처럼 보여서 깔끔합니다.빌트인 설치라 동선 방해도 없고, 기존 싱크 옆 수납장 하나 빼고 쏙 들어가서 공간 활용 면에서도 만족.2. 용량 & 내부 구조14인용이라 처음엔 “우리 집에 너무 큰 거 아닌가?” 했는데, 써보니까 이 정도는 돼야 한 끼 설거지 모아서 한 번에 돌리기 좋더라구요.상단(컵/머그/소형 볼), 중단(그릇/찬기), 하단(냄비/팬/도마) 구조로 되어 있고,칸칸이 높이 조절, 접이식 바스켓이 있어서 집마다 쓰는 그릇 형태에 맞게 조금씩 세팅해두면 편해요.밥공기, 국그릇, 접시, 유리컵, 아이 식판까지 꽉 채워도 한 번에 들어가는 날이 많아서, 손 설거지로 치면 제법 “산더미 설거지”를 기계 한 번으로 끝내는 느낌입니다.3. 세척력 (가장 중요한 부분)기름기 많은 프라이팬, 불고기 양념 그릇, 카레/찌개 그릇까지 테스트해봤는데, 예열 없이 그냥 넣어도 거의 말끔하게 나옵니다.사용 팁:음식물만 살짝 털어내고 넣으면 되고, 굳이 박박 헹굴 필요 없어요.너무 눌어붙은 건 (특히 계란, 치즈) 살짝만 불려서 넣으면 실패 없이 잘 떨어져요.유리컵에 남던 물자국, 뿌연 막 같은 것도 거의 없어져서 컵이 새것처럼 반짝하는 게 확실히 느껴집니다.4. 건조 & 냄새건조 코스까지 돌리면 상온에 꺼내뒀을 때랑 비슷한 정도로 잘 말라 있어요.(바닥 면적 넓은 플라스틱 밀폐용기는 물방울 조금 남는 정도)문이 자동으로 살짝 열리면서 열기 빼주는 기능 덕분인지 눅눅한 냄새, 비린내 거의 없습니다.내부에서 나는 플라스틱 탑 노즐 냄새도 초반 몇 번 사용 이후엔 신경 안 쓰일 정도.5. 소음 & 사용 편의성돌릴 때 소음은 “세탁기 탈수” 기준으로 보면 한참 덜 하고,거실에서 TV 보는 데 방해 안 되는 수준이라 밤에도 돌리기 괜찮아요.조작부가 상단에 깔끔하게 모여 있고, 코스 선택도 직관적이라처음 식세기 입문해도 설명서 한 번 보면 바로 감 잡습니다.문 열고 닫힐 때 느낌이 탄탄해서 오래 쓸 수 있겠다 싶어요.6. 물/시간/멘탈 절약 효과한 번에 돌리면 물 사용량이 손 설거지보다 적다고 해서 골랐는데, 실제로 설거지통에 물 잔뜩 틀어놓고 하던 버릇 생각하면 심리적으로도 절약하는 기분이에요.가장 큰 장점은 시간 & 체력 세이브.식사 후 설거지 산처럼 쌓여 있어도 그냥 기계에 차곡차곡 넣고 버튼 한 번. 저녁마다 설거지 생각에 한숨 쉬던 게 사라져서, 이게 진짜 삶의 질 차이구나 싶습니다.7. 아쉬운 점(솔직하게)처음 설치할 땐 빌트인이다 보니 설치 일정, 주방 사이즈 체크를 꼼꼼히 봐야 해서 살짝 번거롭긴 했어요.(그래도 기사님이 사이즈 맞게 깔끔하게 마감해주셔서 만족)칸이 넉넉한 대신, 아직 손이 안 익어서 초반엔 배치하는 데 시간이 좀 걸렸어요.몇 번 하다 보니 우리 집 그릇 패턴에 맞는 “내부 배치 템플릿”이 생겨서 지금은 자동 손이 가요.❤️❤️❤️총평식세기 처음 입문하면서 걱정했던 세척력, 소음, 디자인 부분을 전부 잡아준 제품이라 정말 만족합니다.특히 주방 톤 맞추고 싶으신 분, 하루에 설거지량이 꾸준히 나오는 집이라면 LG 디오스 오브제컬렉션 14인용 빌트인 선택하시면 후회 없으실 것 같아요.

Sentence (English): The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.
