Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing.
Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Comments (English): In conclusion, this is a product that makes you wonder why it took me so long to get a dishwasher. I will summarize my thoughts after purchasing my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-person. 1. Design & Built-in satisfaction The nature beige color is a subtle tone that is not too much, so it blends in naturally with the kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and do not stand out, and when the door is closed, it looks neat because it is just a single cabinet. Since it is a built-in installation, it does not obstruct the movement, and I am satisfied with the space utilization because it fits in all but one of the storage cabinets next to the existing sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure Since it is a 14-person unit, I thought at first that it was too big for my house. I did, and after using it, I found that it is good for collecting the dishes for one meal and doing them all at once. It has a structure of top (cups/mugs/small bowls), middle (bowls/side dishes), and bottom (pots/pans/cutting boards), and each compartment has height adjustment and a foldable basket, so it is convenient to set it up a little bit to fit the shape of the dishes used in each household. There are many days when I fill it up with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glasses, and even children's plates, so it feels like I am finishing a mountain of dishes by hand with one machine wash. 3. Cleaning power (the most important part) I tested it on greasy frying pans, bulgogi seasoning bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they came out almost cleanly even without preheating. Usage tips: Just lightly shake off the food and put it in, there's no need to rinse it thoroughly. If something is stuck on (especially eggs and cheese), just soak it slightly and put it in, and it comes off without fail. Almost all the water marks and cloudy films left on the glass cups have disappeared, and you can definitely feel the cups shining like new. 4. Drying & Odor If you run the drying cycle, it dries well enough to be similar to when you left it out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a large bottom area, only a few water droplets remain.) Thanks to the function that automatically opens the door slightly to release the heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. The plastic top nozzle smell coming from the inside is not a concern after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use: The noise level is much lower than that of a washing machine spin-dryer, and it's not so loud that it interferes with watching TV in the living room, so it's okay to use it at night. The controls are neatly grouped at the top, and the course selection is intuitive, so even if it's your first time using a dishwasher, you'll get the hang of it after reading the manual. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I think it will last a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Energy Savings: I chose this because it said that running it at once uses less water than washing dishes by hand, and when I think about how I used to leave a lot of water running in the dishwasher, I feel like I'm saving mentally as well. The biggest advantage is that it saves time and energy. Even if the dishes pile up after a meal, I just put them all in the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to have about doing the dishes every evening have disappeared, and I feel like this is a real difference in the quality of life. 7. Disappointing Points (Honestly) When I first installed it, it was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen size because it was built-in. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size.) Although there is ample space, I am not yet used to it, so it took some time to arrange it in the beginning. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal arrangement template that fits the dish pattern in my house, so now my hands go there automatically. Overall Review I am really satisfied with this product because it took care of all the cleaning power, noise, and design that I was worried about when I first got into dishwashing. Especially if you want to match the kitchen tone or have a house where the number of dishes is constant every day, I don't think you will regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-person built-in.

Sentence (English): I used to wonder, "What dishwasher is worth when you live alone?"
Comments (English): [ Made with my own money ] || ---------------- || I used to wonder, "What dishwasher is worth when you live alone?" Then, when I was exposed to dishwashers through an algorithm, I decided I had to buy one. There were plenty of candidates for a six-person dishwasher, and the price was reasonable. Looking at Cuckoo, SK, and Samsung, I realized the manufacturer was the MyDeer factory in Foshan, China. My current induction range is a Rinnai, but it's a MyDeer Takgar. My recent all-in-one oven was also a MyDeer. I looked for the cheapest option and found this one. Since I bought it directly from Coupang and they even covered repairs for a two-year warranty, there was no reason not to buy it. I paid in the evening and had it installed the next day. Since the water purifier was already installed, it used the existing wiring instead of drilling holes, making installation quicker. It doesn't have many modes. Compared to a Samsung from the same factory, the only options are the temperature range and bottle sterilization. It works well and I can feel the improvement in my quality of life. Just give it a quick wipe with a paper towel and put it back in. There's no detergent dispenser, though. It's called a detergent compartment, but if you just close the door, it slides down, so you can throw it on the bottom wing. If this level of detail is lacking and the price is low, this much is forgivable. The installer was very kind, and he told me that an E4 error might occasionally appear during use, so he told me where to check in that case. If you're a single-person household, if space allows, buy this instead of the 3-person one. For an additional tens of thousands of won from the 310,000 won Minix 3-person one, you can get double the capacity. Comments (English): [ Best dishwasher ] || ---------------- || The dishwasher is well-designed, sleek and very quiet. The app makes it easy to start remotely or monitor the progress of a cycle. My house cleaners called me at work to tell me that the dishwasher wouldn't work, but they just couldnt figure it out. I couldn't either at first. Once you know, it's no problem at all, but doesn't work like any other brand.Would highly recommend.

Sentence (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.
