Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design.
Comments (English): To start with the conclusion, this is a product that makes me wonder why I only just got into the world of dishwashers. Let me summarize my thoughts on getting my first dishwasher, the LG Dios Objet Collection Built-in 14-place setting. 1. Design & Built-in Satisfaction. The Nature Beige color is a subtle tone that isn't too flashy, so it blends naturally with my kitchen furniture. The handles and logo are simple and don't stand out, and when the doors are closed, it looks just like a single cabinet, giving it a neat appearance. Since it's a built-in installation, it doesn't obstruct the flow of movement, and I'm satisfied with space utilization as it fits perfectly by removing one of the existing cabinets next to the sink. 2. Capacity & Internal Structure. At first, I wondered if the 14-place setting was too big for my house, but after using it, I realized this size is necessary to gather a meal's worth of dishes and run them all at once. It is structured with an upper section (cups/mugs/small bowls), a middle section (plates/side dishes), and a lower section (pots/pans/cutting boards). With adjustable compartment heights and a foldable basket, it is convenient to set up the racks to fit the different types of dishes used in each household. There are many days when it fits everything at once, even when fully packed with rice bowls, soup bowls, plates, glass cups, and children's lunch trays; it feels like finishing a mountain of dishes in a single pass with the machine, compared to washing them by hand. 3. Cleaning Power (The most important part). I tested it with greasy frying pans, bulgogi marinade bowls, and curry/stew bowls, and they come out almost spotlessly clean even without preheating. Usage Tip: You just need to lightly shake off any food residue before putting them in; there is no need to scrub vigorously. For heavily burnt-on food (especially eggs or cheese), soaking it briefly before putting it in works flawlessly. Water stains and cloudy films left on glass cups are almost completely gone, and you can definitely feel the cups sparkling like new. 4. Drying & Odor. If you run the drying cycle, the dishes dry to a degree similar to when left out at room temperature. (On plastic airtight containers with a wide bottom surface, only a few water droplets remain.) Perhaps thanks to the feature where the door automatically opens slightly to release heat, there is almost no damp or fishy smell. Even the smell of the plastic top nozzle inside is not noticeable after the first few uses. 5. Noise & Ease of Use. The noise level during operation is significantly lower compared to a washing machine's spin cycle. It is quiet enough not to disturb watching TV in the living room, so it is fine to use even at night. The controls are neatly clustered at the top, and course selection is intuitive. Even if you are new to dishwashers, you will get the hang of it immediately after reading the manual once. The door feels solid when opening and closing, so I feel like I will be able to use it for a long time. 6. Water/Time/Mental Savings. I chose this because it uses less water than hand washing when running a full cycle; considering my habit of filling the sink with water, I actually feel like I am saving money psychologically as well. The biggest advantage is saving time and energy. Even if dishes pile up like a mountain after a meal, I just stack them neatly into the machine and press a button. The sighs I used to make every evening thinking about washing dishes have disappeared, and I realize this is truly a difference in quality of life. 7. Areas for Improvement (Honestly). Since it is a built-in model, the initial installation was a bit of a hassle because I had to carefully check the installation schedule and kitchen dimensions. (However, I am satisfied because the technician finished it neatly to fit the size perfectly.) Although the compartments are spacious, it took some time to arrange the dishes at first because I wasn't used to it yet. After doing it a few times, I developed an internal layout template that fits my dish patterns, so now I use it automatically. Overall review: I am truly satisfied because this product addressed all the concerns I had when first getting into dishwashers—cleaning power, noise, and design. Especially if you want to match your kitchen tone or have a consistent amount of dishes to wash every day, I think you won't regret choosing the LG Dios Objet Collection 14-place setting built-in dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Easy to use with no-penetration installation.
Comments (English): [ I really need to relieve my wife's eczema. ] || ---------------- || Easy to use with no-penetration installation. Quiet operation, even at night. Charcoal gray color creates a sophisticated kitchen. Perfect capacity for a family of three. More storage space than expected. Powerful cleaning power. Hello ^-^ This time, I got to try out the *MINIX 3-Person Mini Dishwasher (Charcoal Gray)* as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. To cut to the chase, this product has changed our evening routine a lot. We're a family of three, and we eat three meals a day, even late-night snacks. With four dishes a day, the kitchen sink was always piled high. My wife has eczema, so I was especially worried about her hands getting chapped and sore every time she did the dishes. No matter how many rubber gloves she wore, her fingertips would crack and bleed from repeated contact with water. So, the first thing I noticed after trying this product for this experience group was that it would make my wife's hands much more comfortable. First of all, installation was incredibly easy. I thought dishwashers would be complicated, like connecting plumbing, but this one is a no-penetration installation, so just plug it in and it's ready to go. Since there's no complicated installation process, it's easy to install in any rental, apartment, or studio apartment. I took it out of the box and ran my first wash in less than 10 minutes. I also loved the design. The charcoal gray color complements my kitchen perfectly, and the size isn't too overwhelming. It doesn't take up much space and feels neat, so it looks neat even next to the dining table. Best of all, it's virtually silent. I expected the dishwasher to hum when it was running, but it actually runs incredibly quietly. I can run it at night while my wife and I watch TV, and even in the kitchen near my kids' bedroom, it doesn't bother me at all. It holds a lot more dishes than I expected. I thought it would be small because it's for three people, but it holds enough for a full day's worth of dishes: rice bowls, soup bowls, side dish plates, spoons, and cups. On days when I even have a late-night snack, I only need to run it twice a day. The interior is designed especially efficiently, so if you just take the time to load the dishes, you can fit quite a few. I'm also very satisfied with the cleaning power. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. It leaves no stains or odors, and after washing, it dries with hot air, leaving them fluffy and soft when you take them out. You can even put them in the cabinet right away. My wife now just puts the dishes in the machine and presses a button, so she rarely gets her hands wet. After using it for a few days, she said her hands are less chapped and much happier. She used to apply ointment every night to her hands because they were so sore, but now she's done. That alone makes this product worth the price. Plus, the water is quiet when it's running, and it uses so little electricity that I don't have to worry about the electricity bill. It also saves a lot of water compared to washing dishes by hand, which is also a big plus for our household budget. Now, I can eat four meals a day without worrying about washing dishes. Since I can just load and run the dishes after meals, the sink stays clean, and the kitchen looks tidy. It's a small change, but it's definitely improved my quality of life. Summary of the good points: Easy installation thanks to the non-porous installation; Luxurious and clean charcoal gray design; Nearly silent, so I can use it at night without any worries; Spacious interior space beyond my expectations; Powerful cleaning power and perfect drying; My wife, who has dry hands, loves that she doesn't have to touch the water; Relieves the stress of washing dishes four times a day; Recommended for: People with a lot of dishes or weak hands; Families of two or three people or dual-income couples; Looking for a dishwasher that's easy to install without the porous installation; People who prefer a quiet and clean design. Thanks to this product, our house has been completely freed from the dishwashing war. My wife, who has dry hands, rarely has to dip her hands in water anymore, which is a huge relief. Kitchen life is effortless, even after four meals a day, thanks to the Minix dishwasher. ^^ This review was written after receiving the product free of charge as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

*미닉스 3인용 미니 식기세척기 (차콜 그레이)*를 써보게 됐습니다.  결론부터 말하자면, 이 제품 덕분에 우리 집의 저녁 풍경이 많이 달라졌어요. 저희 집은 세 식구인데, 하루 세 끼는 기본이고 야식까지 챙겨 먹는 편이에요. 하루에 네 번 설거지를 하다 보니 주방 싱크대는 늘 그릇이 쌓여 있었고, 특히 아내가 손습진이 있어서 설거지를 할 때마다 손이 꽂으면 바로 사용할 수 있더라고요. 복잡한 설치 과정이 없으니까, 전세나 아파트, 원룸 어디서든 쉽게 놓을 수 있어요. 박스에서 꺼내서 10분도 안 돼서 첫 세척을 돌렸습니다.  디자인도 마음에 들었어요. 차콜 그레이 색상이 주방에 딱 어울리고, 크기도 부담스럽지 않아요. 공간을 차지하지 않고 딱 정돈된 느낌이라, 식탁 옆에 두어도 깔끔해 보여요.  무엇보다 소음이 거의 없어요. 식기세척기 돌릴 때 ‘웅~’ 하는 소리가 날 줄 알았는데, 실제로는 아주 조용하게 작동합니다. 밤에 아내랑 TV 보면서 돌려도 전혀 거슬리지 않고, 아이가 자는 방과 가까운 주방인데도 전혀 방해되지 않아요.  그릇은 생각보다 훨씬 많이 들어갑니다. 이게 3인용이라 해서 작은 줄 알았는데, 막상 써보니까 밥그릇, 국그릇, 반찬접시, 수저, 컵까지 하루 한 끼 분량은 충분히 들어가요. 야식까지 챙겨 먹는 날은 하루 두 번 돌리면 끝이에요. 특히 내부 공간이 효율적으로 설계되어 있어서, 그릇을 조금만 신경 써서 넣으면 꽤 많이 들어갑니다.  세척력도 아주 만족스럽습니다. 처음엔 솔직히 반신반의했어요. “손으로 닦는 게 더 깨끗하지 않을까?” 싶었는데, 고기 굽고 남은 기름 묻은 접시나 국물 말라붙은 그릇까지 말끔하게 세척돼서 깜짝 놀랐어요. 물때나 냄새도 남지 않고, 세척이 끝나면 뜨거운 바람으로 건조까지 해줘서 꺼낼 때 뽀송뽀송하게 마무리돼요. 바로 수납장에 넣어도 될 정도로요.  아내는 이제 설거지 대신 그릇만 기계에 넣고 버튼만 누르면 되니까 손에 물 닿을 일이 거의 없어졌어요. 며칠 써보더니 “손이 덜 갈라져서 너무 With four dishes a day, the kitchen sink was always piled high. My wife has eczema, so I was especially worried about her hands getting chapped and sore every time she did the dishes. It doesn't take up much space and feels neat, so it looks neat even next to the dining table. Best of all, it's virtually silent. I can run it at night while my wife and I watch TV, and even in the kitchen near my kids' bedroom, it doesn't bother me at all. It holds a lot more dishes than I expected. I thought it would be small because it's for three people, but it holds enough for a full day's worth of dishes: rice bowls, soup bowls, side dish plates, spoons, and cups. On days when I even have a late-night snack, I only need to run it twice a day. The interior is designed especially efficiently, so if you just take the time to load the dishes, you can fit quite a few. I'm also very satisfied with the cleaning power. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. Hello ^-^ This time, I got to try out the *MINIX 3-Person Mini Dishwasher (Charcoal Gray)* as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. To cut to the chase, this product has changed our evening routine a lot. We're a family of three, and we eat three meals a day, even late-night snacks. With four dishes a day, the kitchen sink was always piled high. My wife has eczema, so I was especially worried about her hands getting chapped and sore every time she did the dishes. No matter how many rubber gloves she wore, her fingertips would crack and bleed from repeated contact with water. So, the first thing I noticed after trying this product for this experience group was that it would make my wife's hands much more comfortable. First of all, installation was incredibly easy. I thought dishwashers would be complicated, like connecting plumbing, but this one is a no-penetration installation, so just plug it in and it's ready to go. Since there's no complicated installation process, it's easy to install in any rental, apartment, or studio apartment. I took it out of the box and ran my first wash in less than 10 minutes. I also loved the design. The charcoal gray color complements my kitchen perfectly, and the size isn't too overwhelming. It doesn't take up much space and feels neat, so it looks neat even next to the dining table. Best of all, it's virtually silent. I expected the dishwasher to hum when it was running, but it actually runs incredibly quietly. I can run it at night while my wife and I watch TV, and even in the kitchen near my kids' bedroom, it doesn't bother me at all. It holds a lot more dishes than I expected. I thought it would be small because it's for three people, but it holds enough for a full day's worth of dishes: rice bowls, soup bowls, side dish plates, spoons, and cups. On days when I even have a late-night snack, I only need to run it twice a day. The interior is designed especially efficiently, so if you just take the time to load the dishes, you can fit quite a few. I'm also very satisfied with the cleaning power. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. It leaves no stains or odors, and after washing, it dries with hot air, leaving them fluffy and soft when you take them out. You can even put them in the cabinet right away. My wife now just puts the dishes in the machine and presses a button, so she rarely gets her hands wet. After using it for a few days, she said her hands are less chapped and much happier. She used to apply ointment every night to her hands because they were so sore, but now she's done. That alone makes this product worth the price. Plus, the water is quiet when it's running, and it uses so little electricity that I don't have to worry about the electricity bill. It also saves a lot of water compared to washing dishes by hand, which is also a big plus for our household budget. Now, I can eat four meals a day without worrying about washing dishes. Since I can just load and run the dishes after meals, the sink stays clean, and the kitchen looks tidy. It's a small change, but it's definitely improved my quality of life. Summary of the good points: Easy installation thanks to the non-porous installation; Luxurious and clean charcoal gray design; Nearly silent, so I can use it at night without any worries; Spacious interior space beyond my expectations; Powerful cleaning power and perfect drying; My wife, who has dry hands, loves that she doesn't have to touch the water; Relieves the stress of washing dishes four times a day; Recommended for: People with a lot of dishes or weak hands; Families of two or three people or dual-income couples; Looking for a dishwasher that's easy to install without the porous installation; People who prefer a quiet and clean design. Thanks to this product, our house has been completely freed from the dishwashing war. My wife, who has dry hands, rarely has to dip her hands in water anymore, which is a huge relief. Kitchen life is effortless, even after four meals a day, thanks to the Minix dishwasher. ^^ This review was written after receiving the product free of charge as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. She used to apply ointment every night to her hands because they were so sore, but now she's done. That alone makes this product worth the price. Plus, the water is quiet when it's running, and it uses so little electricity that I don't have to worry about the electricity bill. It also saves a lot of water compared to washing dishes by hand, which is also a big plus for our household budget. Now, I can eat four meals a day without worrying about washing dishes. Since I can just load and run the dishes after meals, the sink stays clean, and the kitchen looks tidy. It's a small change, but it's definitely improved my quality of life. Thanks to this product, our house has been completely freed from the dishwashing war. My wife, who has dry hands, rarely has to dip her hands in water anymore, which is a huge relief. Kitchen life is effortless, even after four meals a day, thanks to the Minix dishwasher. ^^ This review was written after receiving the product free of charge as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

좋다”고 하더라고요. 예전엔 저녁마다 손이 따갑다고 연고 바르고 자곤 했는데, 이제는 그런 말이 사라졌어요. 그거 하나만으로도 이 제품은 값어치를 충분히 한다고 생각합니다.  그리고 이게 작동할 때 물소리도 조용하고, 전기세 걱정도 안 될 정도로 전력 소모가 적어요. 손으로 설거지할 때보다 물도 훨씬 아낄 수 있어서 가계에도 도움이 됩니다.  지금은 하루 To cut to the chase, this product has changed our evening routine a lot. We're a family of three, and we eat three meals a day, even late-night snacks. With four dishes a day, the kitchen sink was always piled high. My wife has eczema, so I was especially worried about her hands getting chapped and sore every time she did the dishes. No matter how many rubber gloves she wore, her fingertips would crack and bleed from repeated contact with water. So, the first thing I noticed after trying this product for this experience group was that it would make my wife's hands much more comfortable. First of all, installation was incredibly easy. I thought dishwashers would be complicated, like connecting plumbing, but this one is a no-penetration installation, so just plug it in and it's ready to go. Since there's no complicated installation process, it's easy to install in any rental, apartment, or studio apartment. I took it out of the box and ran my first wash in less than 10 minutes. I also loved the design. The charcoal gray color complements my kitchen perfectly, and the size isn't too overwhelming. It doesn't take up much space and feels neat, so it looks neat even next to the dining table. Best of all, it's virtually silent. I expected the dishwasher to hum when it was running, but it actually runs incredibly quietly. I can run it at night while my wife and I watch TV, and even in the kitchen near my kids' bedroom, it doesn't bother me at all. It holds a lot more dishes than I expected. I thought it would be small because it's for three people, but it holds enough for a full day's worth of dishes: rice bowls, soup bowls, side dish plates, spoons, and cups. On days when I even have a late-night snack, I only need to run it twice a day. The interior is designed especially efficiently, so if you just take the time to load the dishes, you can fit quite a few. I'm also very satisfied with the cleaning power. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. It leaves no stains or odors, and after washing, it dries with hot air, leaving them fluffy and soft when you take them out. You can even put them in the cabinet right away. My wife now just puts the dishes in the machine and presses a button, so she rarely gets her hands wet. After using it for a few days, she said her hands are less chapped and much happier. She used to apply ointment every night to her hands because they were so sore, but now she's done. That alone makes this product worth the price. Plus, the water is quiet when it's running, and it uses so little electricity that I don't have to worry about the electricity bill. It also saves a lot of water compared to washing dishes by hand, which is also a big plus for our household budget. Now, I can eat four meals a day without worrying about washing dishes. Since I can just load and run the dishes after meals, the sink stays clean, and the kitchen looks tidy. It's a small change, but it's definitely improved my quality of life. Summary of the good points: Easy installation thanks to the non-porous installation; Luxurious and clean charcoal gray design; Nearly silent, so I can use it at night without any worries; Spacious interior space beyond my expectations; Powerful cleaning power and perfect drying; My wife, who has dry hands, loves that she doesn't have to touch the water; Relieves the stress of washing dishes four times a day; Recommended for: People with a lot of dishes or weak hands; Families of two or three people or dual-income couples; Looking for a dishwasher that's easy to install without the porous installation; People who prefer a quiet and clean design. Thanks to this product, our house has been completely freed from the dishwashing war. My wife, who has dry hands, rarely has to dip her hands in water anymore, which is a huge relief. Kitchen life is effortless, even after four meals a day, thanks to the Minix dishwasher. ^^ This review was written after receiving the product free of charge as part of a Coupang Experience Group event.

Hello ^-^ This time, I got to try out the *MINIX 3-Person Mini Dishwasher (Charcoal Gray)* as part of the Coupang Experience Group event. To cut to the chase, this product has changed our evening routine a lot. We're a family of three, and we eat three meals a day, even late-night snacks. With four dishes a day, the kitchen sink was always piled high. My wife has eczema, so I was especially worried about her hands getting chapped and sore every time she did the dishes. No matter how many rubber gloves she wore, her fingertips would crack and bleed from repeated contact with water. So, the first thing I noticed after trying this product for this experience group was that it would make my wife's hands much more comfortable. First of all, installation was incredibly easy. I thought dishwashers would be complicated, like connecting plumbing, but this one is a no-penetration installation, so just plug it in and it's ready to go. Since there's no complicated installation process, it's easy to install in any rental, apartment, or studio apartment. I took it out of the box and ran my first wash in less than 10 minutes. I also loved the design. The charcoal gray color complements my kitchen perfectly, and the size isn't too overwhelming. It doesn't take up much space and feels neat, so it looks neat even next to the dining table. Best of all, it's virtually silent. I expected the dishwasher to hum when it was running, but it actually runs incredibly quietly. I can run it at night while my wife and I watch TV, and even in the kitchen near my kids' bedroom, it doesn't bother me at all. It holds a lot more dishes than I expected. I thought it would be small because it's for three people, but it holds enough for a full day's worth of dishes: rice bowls, soup bowls, side dish plates, spoons, and cups. On days when I even have a late-night snack, I only need to run it twice a day. The interior is designed especially efficiently, so if you just take the time to load the dishes, you can fit quite a few. I'm also very satisfied with the cleaning power. Honestly, I was skeptical at first. I thought washing by hand would be cleaner, but I was pleasantly surprised by how thoroughly it cleaned even the greasy dishes from grilled meats and the ones with dried soup. It leaves no stains or odors, and after washing, it dries with hot air, leaving them fluffy and soft when you take them out. You can even put them in the cabinet right away. My wife now just puts the dishes in the machine and presses a button, so she rarely gets her hands wet. After using it for a few days, she said her hands are less chapped and much happier. She used to apply ointment every night to her hands because they were so sore, but now she's done. That alone makes this product worth the price. Plus, the water is quiet when it's running, and it uses so little electricity that I don't have to worry about the electricity bill. It also saves a lot of water compared to washing dishes by hand, which is also a big plus for our household budget. Now, I can eat four meals a day without worrying about washing dishes. Since I can just load and run the dishes after meals, the sink stays clean, and the kitchen looks tidy. It's a small change, but it's definitely improved my quality of life. Sentence (English): Brand Selection: I chose Midea, a well-known Chinese home appliance brand.
Comments (English): Brand Selection: I chose Midea, a well-known Chinese home appliance brand. Based on my 7-8 years of experience living in China, I purchased it because I recognized it as the LG of the home appliance industry. The cleaning performance is virtually identical to hand-washing. Very satisfied. However, dishes with caked-on seasoning or rice cakes sometimes remain on the dishwasher, requiring pre-rinsing. I've heard this is common in other dishwashers. Detergent Recommendation: I felt that using a tablet (such as a 3-in-1) rather than liquid detergent cleaned the dishes much better. While the exact reason is unknown, I suspect it's due to the tablet's integrated detergent, rinse, and drying agent structure. Suitable Dish Type: This model is a 6-person model, making it more suitable for a setup with a focus on flat plates. Large bowls and pots are limited, requiring separate hand washing. Therefore, a setup with large bowls and flat plates would be more efficient. Overall Review: Very satisfied. It offers excellent value for money, and I would consider purchasing another appliance in the future. If this review was helpful, please click "helpful"! Thank you!
Comments (Original): ✅브랜드 선택 중국에서 유명한 가전 브랜드인 Midea(미디어)을 선택함. 중국 거주 7~8년 경험 바탕으로 “가전계의 LG급”이라는 인식으로 구매.  ✅세척력  손 설거지와 거의 차이 없음. 매우 만족. 다만 양념이 굳거나 밥풀이 붙은 접시는 한 번 남는 경우 있어, 사전 헹굼이 필요함. 듣기론 이런 상황은 다른 식기세척기에서도 유사하다는 의견 있음.  ✅세제 추천  액체세제보다는 타블릿형 세제 (3-in-1 등 복합형) 사용 시 훨씬 잘 닦이는 체감. 이유는 정확히 모르지만 “타블릿 = 세제+린스+건조제 일체형” 구조 때문으로 추정  ✅적합한 식기 타입  본 제품이 “6인용” 모델로, 평면 접시 위주 구성에 더 적합함. 큰 그릇이나 냄비는 많이 제한되어 있어 별도 손 설거지가 필요했음. 따라서 “큰 그릇 ↓, 평면 접시 ↑” 식으로 구성하면 효율 ↑.  ✅총평  결론적으로 매우 만족함. 가성비 우수하고, 향후 가전 구매 시에도 다시 고려할 의사 있음.  ✅리뷰가 도움되면 도움이 돼요 한번씩 눌러주세요! 감사합니다 ^^

Sentence (English): I chose Midea, a well-known Chinese home appliance brand.
Comments (English): I chose Midea, a well-known Chinese home appliance brand. Based on my 7-8 years of experience living in China, I purchased it because I recognized it as the LG of the home appliance industry. The cleaning power is virtually identical to hand washing, and I'm very satisfied. However, some dishes with caked-on seasoning or rice cakes may remain, requiring a pre-rinse. I've heard this happens with other dishwashers as well. Detergent Recommendation: I felt that using a tablet (such as a 3-in-1) rather than liquid detergent cleaned the dishes much better. While the exact reason is unknown, I suspect it's due to the tablet's integrated detergent, rinse, and drying agent structure. Suitable Dish Type: This model is a 6-person model, making it more suitable for a setup with a focus on flat plates. Larger dishes and pots are limited, requiring separate hand washing. Therefore, a setup with large bowls and flat plates would be more efficient. Overall: Very satisfied. It offers excellent value for money, and I would consider purchasing another appliance in the future. If this review was helpful, please click "helpful"! Thank you ^^

Sentence (English): Brand selection.
Comments (English): Brand selection. I chose Midea, a well-known home appliance brand in China. Based on my 7-8 years of experience living in China, I purchased it because I recognized it as the LG of the home appliance industry. Cleaning performance: Almost the same as hand washing. Very satisfied. However, dishes with caked-on seasoning or rice cakes sometimes remain on the dishwasher, requiring pre-rinsing. I've heard this happens with other dishwashers as well. Detergent recommendation: I felt that using a tablet (such as a 3-in-1) cleaned much better than liquid detergent. This model is a 6-person model, making it more suitable for a setup with a focus on flat plates. Large bowls and pots are limited, requiring separate hand washing. Therefore, a setup with large bowls and flat plates would be more efficient. Overall review: Very satisfied. It's cost-effective, and I would consider purchasing another appliance. Comments (English): [ Super-quiet and washes well - with finicky control ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher is incredibly quiet, being barely if at all noticeable when it is in operation. The dishwashing capability is also excellent, better than any dishwasher we have ever owned. This model essentially checks all boxes as a dishwasher except one, and this exception is enough to cause one star getting knocked off. The control panel on the top of the door is temperamental and finicky. Just six months into the ownership the panel went berzerk (all lit up) and froze up, and requiring multiple hard resets at the power source before coming back to life. The capacitive buttons act like many of those automobile dash screens - not very responsive and inconsistent when they do respond. For this price, we wish Bosch had put more attention to this part of the hardware in an otherwise nearly perfect dishwasher.

Sentence (English): Washes the dishes perfectly.
Comments (English): [ High quality and design, with some caveats ] || ---------------- || Washes the dishes perfectly. Efficient, uses little water and electricity. The internal light is very useful. Shelves have complex shapes, providing positions for quality washing of kitchen stuff of all shapes. The latter comes at a price: capacity is much smaller than that of a dishwasher with standard shelves. A 26" pan won't fit sideways under any circumstance, has to be laid flat. This dishwasher cannot operate with the middle shelf removed, unlike the majority of American brands, limiting the ability to wash larger objects. This is clearly an improvement opportunity for Samsung, as technically enabling that is easy.Installation is a beast. Hose outlets are about 2.5" above floor, meaning you'll need to cut a hole in the wall of the cabinet in the base, below the cabinet floor, and in the cabinet floor. The included printed installation manual is way too abridged, be sure to get the online version that speaks in detail about this issue.If installing on a drip pan, make sure that side walls of the pan don't wedge between the frame of the dishwasher and the walls of cabinets around - when it gets stuck, pulling it out becomes a challenge. Trim these drip pan side walls to size before sliding the dishwasher in.Water supply requires a 90 degree elbow to be purchased separately. I'd recommend choosing a supply water line that has such an elbow built-in, w/o adapters and such, because the inlet is so near the floor and side that there is not enough clearance for the line if using an adaptor. This can be solved by orienting the elbow towards the center of the dishwasher and then turning the hose 180 degrees using the available space behind the frame, but why fiddle with that if there is an easier way? Build quality looks very high. The appliance is fully enclosed, including on the bottom, and is equipped with a leak sensor. At the discounted price, it is a solid alternative to Bosch, if the capacity limitations are acceptable.

The latter comes at a price: capacity is much smaller than that of a dishwasher with standard shelves. A 26" pan won't fit sideways under any circumstance, has to be laid flat. This is clearly an improvement opportunity for Samsung, as technically enabling that is easy.Installation is a beast. Trim these drip pan side walls to size before sliding the dishwasher in.Water supply requires a 90 degree elbow to be purchased separately. I'd recommend choosing a supply water line that has such an elbow built-in, w/o adapters and such, because the inlet is so near the floor and side that there is not enough clearance for the line if using an adaptor. This can be solved by orienting the elbow towards the center of the dishwasher and then turning the hose 180 degrees using the available space behind the frame, but why fiddle with that if there is an easier way? Build quality looks very high. The appliance is fully enclosed, including on the bottom, and is equipped with a leak sensor. At the discounted price, it is a solid alternative to Bosch, if the capacity limitations are acceptable.

Sentence (English): I recently owned a KitchenAid dishwasher, and overall, it's a strong, dependable appliance that does what it's supposed to do — and does it well.
Comments (English): I recently owned a KitchenAid dishwasher, and overall, it's a strong, dependable appliance that does what it's supposed to do — and does it well. The first thing that stands out is how quiet it runs. Even on the heavy wash cycle, you can barely hear it. If you have an open kitchen or do work nearby, that's a big plus.In terms of cleaning power, it performs great. Dishes, glasses, and even pots with dried food come out spotless most of the time. I especially like the third rack, which makes it easy to load utensils and smaller items without wasting space on the bottom racks. The stainless-steel interior also feels sturdy and gives it a high-end look.There are a few small downsides, though. The price is on the higher side compared to other brands, so it's definitely an investment. Also, like many dishwashers, it sometimes struggles to completely dry plastic items — cups or containers might still have a few drops left on them after the cycle ends.Still, the pros outweigh the cons. It's quiet, efficient, and looks great in the kitchen. If you want a reliable, long-lasting dishwasher and don't mind paying a little more for quality, a KitchenAid dishwasher is a solid choice.

Sentence (English): I recently owned a KitchenAid dishwasher, and overall, it's a strong, dependable appliance that does what it's supposed to do — and does it well.
Comments (English): I recently owned a KitchenAid dishwasher, and overall, it's a strong, dependable appliance that does what it's supposed to do — and does it well. The first thing that stands out is how quiet it runs. Even on the heavy wash cycle, you can barely hear it. If you have an open kitchen or do work nearby, that's a big plus. In terms of cleaning power, it performs great. Dishes, glasses, and even pots with dried food come out spotless most of the time. I especially like the third rack, which makes it easy to load utensils and smaller items without wasting space on the bottom racks. The stainless-steel interior also feels sturdy and gives it a high-end look. There are a few small downsides, though. The price is on the higher side compared to other brands, so it's definitely an investment. Also, like many dishwashers, it sometimes struggles to completely dry plastic items — cups or containers might still have a few drops left on them after the cycle ends. Still, the pros outweigh the cons. It's quiet, efficient, and looks great in the kitchen. If you want a reliable, long-lasting dishwasher and don't mind paying a little more for quality, a KitchenAid dishwasher is a solid choice.

Sentence (English): Since getting the Minix Mini Dishwasher PRO 3-Person MNDW-110CG in Charcoal Gray, my dishwashing routine has completely changed.
Comments (English): Since getting the Minix Mini Dishwasher PRO 3-Person MNDW-110CG in Charcoal Gray, my dishwashing routine has completely changed. Simply rinse the dishes, place them upright in the basket, and press a button. It's a breeze to do after work, saving me time and energy. I was worried about having to install it myself, but it was quick and easy: just connect the included hose, drain the dishwasher, and drain it into the sink. The matte charcoal color blends seamlessly into my kitchen. It doesn't take up much countertop space, making it a great choice for a single-room or small kitchen. The standard cycle cleans up grease and liquid stains, and the powerful cycle even tackled stuck-on saucepans. The evenly distributed water from the rotating nozzle significantly reduced water marks on the bottom of cups, and adding rinse aid makes glasses shine even more. The noise level is mostly the sound of running water, so it's barely noticeable when the TV is on. Leaving the door slightly open after washing reduces odors and moisture by allowing the residual heat to dry. The well-designed basket makes it easy to set up dishes. Large plates stacked one on top of the other, and bowls placed with the opening facing down helped reduce water pooling. For heavily seasoned dishes, I simply swept them with a paper towel to maintain the filter. Rinsing the nozzle and filter once a week keeps performance stable. Even just running it once or twice a day noticeably reduces sink clutter, and it significantly saves water and detergent, making it a great value. In short, it's a great model that keeps things neat and tidy even in a small kitchen. Once you get used to it, you'll notice a significant reduction in the amount of hand washing. More important than my intention to repurchase, I plan to take it with me on my next move.

Sentence (English): Even with a small family, the weekends can be tiring with the amount of dishes to do.
Comments (English): Even with a small family, the weekends can be tiring with the amount of dishes to do. And crucially, the lack of drying space after washing dishes leaves a lot of moisture around the sink, which is why I bought this. Of course, I still need to pre-wash and put it in the dishwasher, but since I can wash and dry it in the dishwasher, I don't have to stress about lack of drying space. And since I added the hot air drying function to the automatic drying function, there don't seem to be many water stains. So I use a detergent that doubles as a rinse aid (one tablet for 6 people) and don't add salt. I was worried about the hot air function, but I think it's a good idea to have it. ^^
Comments (Original): 주말에는 식구가 적더라도 설거지 양이 많아 힘들기도 하고, 결정적으로 설거지를 하고 난후 건조공간이 부족해 싱크대 주변이 물기가 많아서 구입하게 되었어요. 물론 애벌세척을 하고 식세기에 돌려야 하지만, 식세기에서 세척하고 건조까지 가능하니 건조공간 부족한 스트레스도 없고 좋네요. 그리고 자동건조에 열풍 건조 기능을 추가해서 돌리니 물자국이 별로 없는듯해요. 그래서 린스겸용 세제(6인용 1알) 사용하고, 소금추가 없이 사용하고 있어요. 열풍기능 고민했는데 있는게 괜찮은것 같아요^^

Sentence (English): My new black slate dishwasher from GE has performed admirably so far.
Comments (English): My new black slate dishwasher from GE has performed admirably so far. It's very quiet and has cleaned everything well. I scrape dishes, no rinsing, and add them though I don't put pots, pans, or baking sheets into the dishwasher. I LOVE the black slate finish. It doesn't flash at you like the stainless steel or show smudges or streaks. It's a better fit for the colors of my kitchen. After the delivery guys left, I realized that there was a scratch underneath a sticker on the handle. I called Home Depot the next day. There was no challenge to my claim. They immediately sent a new handle out which was very easy for me to swap out. I'm not happy about the scratch (it was about 4 inches) but they were so responsive that I'm not holding it against the dishwasher's rating.

Sentence (English): My dishwasher is 3 years and 6 months old.
Comments (English): [ It works well, until it stops working ] || ---------------- || My dishwasher is 3 years and 6 months old. It's been used normally by a family of three. Suddenly, the thing starts making a terrible noise. Well, the motor is broken. Since it "supposedly" has a 10-year warranty on the motor, I figured, well, they'll replace it. And sure enough, they do, "but" I have to pay for the installer's travel and labor. So the only reasonable option is to pay a whopping €149 for the "Peace of Mind" plan. A plan I also paid for a few months ago to fix an LG refrigerator that was also 3 years and 8 months old. So, I'm "VERY HAPPY" with the brand and its €150 surcharge on its products.

Tarifa que también he pagado hace unos meses para arreglar un frigorífico LG que también tenía 3 años y 8 meses. Así que 'MUY CONTENTO' con la marca y su sobre-coste de 150€ en sus productos.

Sentence (English): We previously had a NEFF dishwasher that broke down after nine years.

Well, it's like going from a Mercedes to a Dacia. Both are made by BSH, I know. But hey, you could barely hear the NEFF, but with the Bosch, you can hear the water splashing all the way up to the first floor. It's incredibly loud. Then there's the fact that the tub inside is made of plastic. I've never seen that before. And the Bosch brand doesn't even come with a salt dispenser anymore. Oh well, the next one will probably be a Samsung.

Naja, der nächste wir wohl ein Samsung werden.

Sentence (English): What a cheap, pathetic machine!
Comments (English): [ A Lemon That Keeps On Leaking (and Breaking) ] || ---------------- || What a cheap, pathetic machine! This so-called “washer” is under one year old and I've already had the tech out three separate times—each visit more infuriating than the last. I'm not talking about minor hiccups; I'm talking full-on mechanical meltdowns that leave my laundry room looking like a crime scene of suds and despair.First breakdown (Month 3): The drum decided to imitate a dying walrus—clanging, thumping, and refusing to spin. Tech replaced a “faulty bearing.” Cool, fixed. Or so I thought.Second breakdown (Month 7): Mid-cycle, the machine flooded my floor like it was auditioning for a disaster movie. Error code? “Water inlet valve failure.” Another part, another $200 service call (warranty covered the part, not the labor—thanks for nothing).Third breakdown (Month 11): This time it just stopped. No lights, no hum, nothing. Tech's diagnosis? “Main control board fried.” Are you kidding me? This isn't a $99 bargain bin special—this was a “premium” model with all the bells and whistles that apparently short-circuit if you look at them wrong.Three strikes in under 365 days. The warranty is a joke, the customer service reps read from scripts like robots (ironic), and the machine itself is a rolling advertisement for planned obsolescence. Save your money, your sanity, and your socks—buy literally anything else. This washer doesn't clean clothes; it cleans out your wallet and your will to live.

The high-temperature steam also effectively sterilizes dishes, making it a crucial purchase for me, a hygiene-conscious person. It's also incredibly convenient. Even when I have to run the dishwasher late at night, the quiet cycle allows me to use it without worrying about noise. Since the kitchen and living room are connected, I'm sensitive to noise, but this cycle is so quiet it drowns out the noise of everyday life, which is a huge plus. The automatic door-opening feature, which automatically opens after each wash cycle, prevents moisture buildup and allows the dishwasher to air-dry effectively, reducing water stains. I also find the remote control function via a smartphone app very useful. It's very convenient to be able to pre-start the dishwasher when I return home, or to check the dishwashing progress in real time. With just one dishwasher, I get everything from kitchen hygiene to time management and a better quality of life. I definitely recommend it to anyone who's hesitating. Sentence (English): I used to think I could just do the dishes myself, so I left it off my list of appliances.
Comments (English): [ I thought I could just do the dishes ] || ---------------- || I used to think I could just do the dishes myself, so I left it off my list of appliances. But spending so much time and energy on dishes was exhausting while raising a child. I had to do the dishes, and my child would cry and clutch at his pants. I was on the verge of going crazy when I bought a dishwasher. I'm leaving a review right after using it for the first time, and I'm so happy. It's much cleaner and squeakier than my own dishes. The installer was really kind and shared his experience, along with helpful tips and detergent recommendations. The 20-30 minutes I'd spent doing the dishes could be spent on playing with my child, which is the most satisfying part. It's a 12-inch dishwasher, but it's incredibly spacious! I got a 10% discount with the Premium Efficiency Appliances sale, so I got it for a really cheap price. I used the 1-hour, steam, and high-temperature drying cycle, and it took 2 hours and 12 minutes. Since I eat a lot of greasy food, he said I could usually do regular dishes without steaming, which takes about 1 hour and 40 minutes. About 15 minutes before the end time, the door automatically opens and the high-temperature drying begins. Sentence (English): We purchased our model 300 Bosch dishwasher to replace a Samsung washer that started leaking on the floor during use.
Comments (English): [ Our 1st Bosch appliance ] || ---------------- || We purchased our model 300 Bosch dishwasher to replace a Samsung washer that started leaking on the floor during use. Our first use of the 300 did not go very well. We immediately received an error message stating that the washer would not drain properly. A problem that we never had with our old unit. We needed to have a service call to fix the issue. It turned out to be the drain vent was partially obstructed. After cleaning the vent the problem went away. The dishes clean fine now except the plastic items come out wet even with the extra dry option selected. I am pleased with the 300 now. It does a good job even on baked on food on pans. The front panel lights are a feature that I chose the 300 on. It is nice to see where the wash cycle is during use. The 3rd tray for silverware is great too.
